findings.title: Wrap app imports in thunks so the app store actually loads lazily
Stop using `forEach(async …)`, which escapes the try/catch and leaves promises dangling
`getCalendarCredentials` now returns a Promise in `calendar`, which may break other callers

true_positives.golden_comment: Consider adding try-catch around the await to handle import failures gracefully
true_positives.matched_candidate: If any app module fails to load, the rejected promise sits in the map as an unhandled rejection, which can crash Node processes even when the failing app is never used
true_positives.reasoning: Both comments identify the same underlying issue: the lack of error handling for the async import/load operation. The golden comment suggests adding try-catch to handle import failures gracefully, while the candidate issue points out that failed module loads result in unhandled rejections that can crash Node processes. Both are concerned with the same problem - missing error handling for potential import failures - just expressed differently.

true_positives.golden_comment: The code uses forEach with async callbacks, which causes asynchronous operations (e.g., calendar/video event deletions, payment refunds) to run concurrently without being awaited. This 'fire-and-forget' behavior leads to unhandled promise rejections, race conditions, and incomplete cleanup, as surrounding try-catch blocks cannot properly handle errors from these unawaited promises. Replace forEach with for...of loops or Promise.all() with map() to ensure proper sequential execution and error handling.
true_positives.matched_candidate: Using forEach with async callbacks causes errors to escape the try/catch block, resulting in unhandled rejections from getCalendar, deleteEvent, or deleteMeeting calls
true_positives.reasoning: The candidate issue identifies the same core problem as the golden comment: using forEach with async callbacks causes errors to escape the try/catch block, resulting in unhandled promise rejections. The candidate specifically mentions the same concern about async operations (getCalendar, deleteEvent, deleteMeeting) not being properly awaited and errors not being caught. While the golden comment provides more detail about consequences (race conditions, incomplete cleanup) and solutions (for...of or Promise.all with map), both identify the same fundamental bug.

false_positives.candidate: App imports are not wrapped in thunks, causing all 29 app packages to load eagerly when @calcom/app-store is imported instead of loading lazily as intended
Each app package being split into its own async chunk adds bundling overhead

Using forEach with async callbacks means nothing waits for calendar and video deletions to complete before the handler continues with emails, DB updates, and response, causing race conditions and silently dropped failures

getCalendarCredentials now returns a Promise in the calendar field, which will break other callers that check if (calendar) or call calendar.method() since they will see a truthy Promise instead of the actual calendar object
